title: add-model-invocation-energy-telemetry-and-trace-anchoring
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: Add fine-grained per-invocation energy attribution and lightweight trace anchors so oncall and SRE can correlate inference latency/cost regressions with measured GPU/host energy variation across Dedicated clusters. This change introduces energy-metering annotations derived from node-level power samples, ties meters to invocation traces via a stable anchor ID, and surfaces the data in a new dashboard and a low-noise alert for energy drift. Summary of changes: 1) runtime/telemetry: new invocation_energy meter computed as sum(joules) across scheduled device intervals; exported as metric redwood.invocation.energy_joules with labels {model, model_version, tenant, gpu_type, hw_split, invocation_phase}. 2) tracing: inject trace anchor (trace_anchor_id) into span metadata and attach a short energy sample digest (min/median/max joules over invocation) as span attributes for quick triage. 3) observability: Grafana dashboard 'Inference Energy Explorer' with per-model sparklines, percentile cohorting, and an energy drift panel that shows model-level energy per-token over time. 4) alerts: new alert rule energy-drift-high which triggers when median energy per-token increases by >25% over baseline for 10m and is evidence-backed by >500 invocations in the window. 5) sampling and costs: energy attributes are stamped only for sampled traces by default (1%) to limit cardinality; a per-tenant opt-in flag enables 100% sampling for Dedicated customers. 6) tests & docs: unit tests for energy aggregation, e2e replaybench with synthetic power traces, and developer docs describing how anchors map to traces and billing reports. Checklist: - [x] Telemetry metric schema defined and registered - [x] Runtime aggregation implemented with microbenchmarks - [x] Tracing attribute injection and anchor propagation - [x] Grafana panels and dashboard JSON added - [x] Alert rule and playbook drafted - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Dev docs and migration notes Non-goals: This PR does not change billing pipelines or cost accounting; energy_joules is advisory for now and will be used as an ops signal only. Commits summary: - Add energy sampler and aggregator to runtime (5 commits) - Trace anchor propagation and span attribute encoder (3 commits) - Add Grafana dashboard JSON + panels (2 commits) - Alert rule + Prometheus query + runbook (1 commit) - Tests and docs (2 commits) Files changed (high-level): - runtime/telemetry/energy_sampler.go - runtime/telemetry/energy_schema.yaml - runtime/trace/anchor_propagator.go - runtime/trace/span_encoder.go - observability/grafana/dashboards/inference_energy_explorer.json - observability/alerts/energy_drift.rule.yaml - observability/playbooks/energy_drift.md - tests/replaybench/energy_replay_test.go - docs/observability/energy_telemetry.md - sdk/ts/examples/energy-anchor-usage.ts - plumbing/metrics/registry.go - deployment/helm/values-observability.yaml - ci/test-e2e-energy.yml - scripts/clients/energy-sim.py Review conversation summary: - Ethan Morales (reviewer): "Can we avoid adding high-cardinality labels on the core metric? model_version and tenant are okay but please don't include full prompt hashes." Author reply (Priya): "Agreed. Metric schema keeps cardinality minimal; prompt hashes were dropped. Added model_stage and hw_split flags only for Dedicated telemetry and behind a config toggle." - Lina Zhang (reviewer): "Alert looks noisy for small tenants. Can we require minimum sample count?" Author reply: "Yes, alert now includes a sample count clause (>500 invocations) and is suppressed below that threshold. Added per-tenant auto-quiet window for low-traffic tenants." - David Perez (approver): "Looks good, small nits in dashboard layout. Approving after nits fixed." - Post-review followup: adjusted panel time ranges, tightened PromQL aggregation windows, and added unit tests for sample-weighting. CI checks: - golangci-lint: pass - unit-tests: pass - integration-e2e-energy: pass (replaybench) - dashboard-lint: pass - helm-lint: pass Observability and operations notes: - Sampling defaults to 1% global to limit ingestion cost; Dedicated tenants can enable 100% sampling via Observability flags in the Console. - trace_anchor_id is a stable 64-bit hex token derived from invocation id and node hash; it is not PII. - The dashboard includes a 'Top contributors' panel that correlates high energy with model stage (embed/decoder), sequence length, and kernel occupancy. - Playbook: when energy-drift-high fires the runbook instructs on checking trace anchors, fetching the short energy digest from the span (via traces UI), and correlating with GPU kernel queueing and host throttling metrics. Migration notes: - Consumers of telemetry should watch for redwood.invocation.energy_joules label schema pinned in runtime/telemetry/energy_schema.yaml. - No downstream billing changes; a follow-up will propose a normalized energy_rate token cost if product approves. Rollout plan: - Canary on staging and 2 Dedicated clusters for two weeks. - Flip sampling toggle for 2 pilot tenants, monitor ingestion and alert noise. - If stable, enable global 1% for Hosted and add docs for Dedicated opt-in. Release notes: "Introduce per-invocation energy telemetry and trace anchoring to aid ops triage for inference regressions. Adds new dashboard and an energy drift alert; sampling defaults to 1%."
